_note: HAND-WRITTEN example in the shape of a real reply, used by --offline. NOT a recording of a model.

findings.quote: route requests to the appropriate track according to the policy, etc.
findings.explanation: "Appropriate" and "etc." leave the routing rules to the implementer. Two implementers will route Figma editor seats or unknown tools differently.
findings.suggested_rewrite: List the rules in order with the first match winning, as in SPEC-006 REQ-4, and one acceptance criterion per rule.

findings.quote: WHEN a manager approves a request, THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it approved.
findings.explanation: Nothing says which manager may approve which request, whether security requests need the security team, or what happens when someone approves their own request.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Split into an authority requirement (who may approve each route) and a refusal requirement (403, request unchanged).

findings.quote: The system should handle invalid input gracefully.
findings.explanation: No status code, error shape or rule for what counts as invalid. One implementer returns 400 with text, another 422 with JSON.
findings.suggested_rewrite: IF the body does not match the contract, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 422 with error code validation_error and SHALL NOT store anything.

findings.quote: store it quickly and return it
findings.explanation: "Quickly" has no number, and "return it" does not say which status code or fields.
findings.suggested_rewrite: respond 201 with the stored request; move speed to an NFR with a p95 target in milliseconds.
